rows.ARS:
Medium red Grandiflora.
Registration name: Samouraï ® (grandiflora, Meilland, 1966)
Exhibition name: Scarlet Knight
rows.Origin:
Bred by Marie-Louise (Louisette) Meilland (Paolino) (1920-1987) (France, before 1966).
Introduced in France by URS (Universal Rose Selection)-Meilland in 1966.
Introduced in Australia by Treloar Roses in 1967 as 'Samouraï'.
Introduced in United States by Conard-Pyle (Star Roses) in 1967.
rows.Bloom: Red, ruby-red shading, purple shading. Mild fragrance. 25 to 30 petals. Average diameter 5". Very large, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, in small clusters, cupped bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Medium, armed with thorns / prickles, bushy, upright. Large, bronze-green, leathery foliage.

Height: 30" to 33" (75 to 85cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Can be used for cut flower or garden. Produces decorative hips. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
rows.Patents: United States - Patent No: PP 2,692 on 13 Dec 1966 VIEW USPTO PATENT

rows.Notes: According to Peter Harris, when 'Scarlet Knight' is used in a rosebreeding program it will produce nearly 100% reds and red bicolors if selfed, which means it's a dominant red/bicolor.
